newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh taka ends weaker on dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh taka ends weaker on dlr demand.

text.p: Increased demand for the U.S. dollar from importers and the central bank's restriction on its own selling forced the Bangladesh taka to close weaker on Monday.
The taka ended at 43.7500/7600 to the dollar in interbank trading, down from the previous close of 43.7475/7495, dealers said.

The local unit opened weaker at 43.7490/7510 and lost further ground amid a widening gap between dollar demand and supply. Dealers said dollar demand from importers shot up with the reopening of international markets.
The interbank call money rates closed at six to seven percent against the previous nine to 10 percent.
